templates.title: Prototype lookup and this binding
templates.prompt: Explain how JavaScript resolves a property through the prototype chain and why extracting a method can change the value of this.
templates.objective: Reason about runtime property lookup and call-site-based this binding without relying on memorized syntax rules.
hints: Separate where a property is found from how a function receives its receiver.
Compare obj.method() with const fn = obj.method; fn().
templates.explanation: Property lookup walks an object's prototype chain until a matching key is found. For ordinary functions, this is determined by the call site; extracting a method removes the receiver unless it is bound or wrapped.
goodAnswerSignals: Separates prototype lookup from this binding
Explains bind, wrapper, or arrow trade-offs
weakAnswerSignals: Says this points to where a function was written
Treats classes as having no prototype behavior
followUpPrompts: How does an arrow function differ here?
When would bind make cleanup harder?
mayaPushbacks: Show the exact call site that changes the receiver.
Property lookup and this are two mechanisms—separate them.

scoringRubric.strong: Correctly separates lookup and receiver binding with a working example.
scoringRubric.developing: Understands one mechanism but mixes the other.
scoringRubric.weak: Uses an incorrect lexical definition of this.

templates.title: TypeScript narrowing at data boundaries
templates.prompt: An API response is typed as unknown. Explain how you would validate and narrow it before the UI uses it, and why a type assertion is not validation.
templates.objective: Protect a runtime trust boundary using validation, narrowing, and an explicit failure path.
hints: unknown prevents property access until evidence narrows the value.
Ask what happens when the server returns a structurally different payload.
templates.explanation: TypeScript types disappear at runtime. Data from a network or storage boundary must be checked with a schema or explicit guards; only the validated result should be narrowed into the application type, with malformed data handled deliberately.
goodAnswerSignals: Uses schema validation or precise guards
weakAnswerSignals: Confuses compile-time checking with runtime validation
followUpPrompts: Where should validation live?
How would you report a partial payload?
mayaPushbacks: What executes at runtime to prove that claim?
Show the malformed-data path.

scoringRubric.strong: Clear runtime trust-boundary model and failure behavior.
scoringRubric.developing: Knows unknown but validation is vague.

templates.title: React keys and state identity
templates.prompt: A reordered editable list shows text under the wrong item. Diagnose how keys affect React state identity and choose a stable fix.
templates.objective: Connect stable keys to component identity, preservation, and intentional reset behavior.
hints: React associates state with a component's position and identity in the rendered tree.
Ask whether the key follows the data item when order changes.
templates.explanation: Index or generated keys can associate an existing component instance with different data after insertion or reorder. A stable domain identifier lets React preserve the right state; changing a key is appropriate only when an intentional reset is desired.
goodAnswerSignals: Explains identity rather than only warning against indexes
Mentions key changes can reset state
followUpPrompts: When is an index key safe?
How would you intentionally reset a form?
mayaPushbacks: Why did the input state move?
What identity survives the reorder?

answerStructure.framework: Symptom → identity → stable key → reset rule

scoringRubric.strong: Accurate state-identity model with stable and reset cases.
scoringRubric.developing: Knows index keys are risky but not why.
scoringRubric.weak: Treats keys as a rendering optimization only.

templates.title: Effect synchronization and request races
templates.prompt: A search screen sometimes shows results for the previous query. Explain the effect lifecycle, dependency, and cleanup strategy that prevents stale responses.
templates.objective: Treat effects as synchronization processes and prevent an older async result from committing after a newer one.
hints: Each query change starts a new synchronization cycle and should stop the old one.
Cancellation and ignoring a stale completion solve related but different parts of the problem.
templates.explanation: The query is reactive and must be a dependency. Before the next synchronization starts, cleanup should abort or invalidate the previous request. The completion path must verify it still belongs to the latest request before committing state.
weakAnswerSignals: Removes the dependency to stop reruns
Only debounces and ignores out-of-order completion
followUpPrompts: Does abort alone guarantee no stale commit?
When would this not need an effect?
mayaPushbacks: Which request is allowed to write state?
What exactly happens during cleanup?

answerStructure.framework: Reactive input → start → cleanup → guarded commit

scoringRubric.strong: Models synchronization and stale completion precisely.
scoringRubric.developing: Uses cleanup but cannot explain the race.
scoringRubric.weak: Suppresses dependencies or relies only on timing.

templates.title: State ownership as a feature grows
templates.prompt: A checkout feature has local input state, shared cart state, server totals, and a multi-step transition. Decide what belongs locally, in a reducer/context, and in server state.
templates.objective: Assign state by ownership and lifecycle instead of placing all changing data in one global store.
hints: Classify each value by source of truth, sharing radius, and persistence lifecycle.
A reducer organizes transitions; context transports a value; neither makes server data authoritative.
templates.explanation: Ephemeral input stays near the component, coordinated client transitions can use a reducer, context can distribute stable shared state, and server-owned totals remain server state with cache and mutation rules. Derived values should not become duplicate state.
weakAnswerSignals: Treats context as a full state model
followUpPrompts: Which total is authoritative?
What survives a route change?
mayaPushbacks: Who owns that value?
Why is that stored instead of derived?

scoringRubric.strong: State placement follows ownership and lifecycle with no duplicate truths.

templates.title: Testing an asynchronous user flow
templates.prompt: Design a reliable test for a form that submits, shows progress, handles a server error, and succeeds on retry without asserting component internals.
templates.objective: Test observable behavior across async state transitions using realistic interaction and controlled network outcomes.
hints: Write the flow in terms of what the user can find, do, and observe.
Control the network boundary and await a visible state transition rather than a timer.
templates.explanation: Render the feature, interact through accessible roles and labels, mock the network boundary, assert progress and error behavior, retry, and await the final visible success. Avoid implementation selectors, arbitrary sleeps, and assertions on internal state.
goodAnswerSignals: Covers error and retry with controlled responses
weakAnswerSignals: Asserts hook state or private methods
followUpPrompts: What belongs in an end-to-end test?
How do you prove duplicate submits are blocked?
mayaPushbacks: What can the user observe?
Why is that wait deterministic?

answerStructure.framework: Arrange boundary → act as user → observe transitions

scoringRubric.strong: Deterministic behavior-focused test across success and recovery.
scoringRubric.developing: Covers the happy path but not reliable transitions.

templates.title: Server and client rendering boundaries
templates.prompt: Design the rendering boundaries for a product page with SEO content, personalized price, an interactive gallery, and a live cart count.
templates.objective: Choose server and client boundaries from data locality, interactivity, caching, payload, and hydration constraints.
hints: Classify each region by whether it needs browser state or event handlers.
Then decide where each data dependency can be fetched and cached.
templates.explanation: Static or request-time content can render on the server, while interactive islands own browser state. Keep the client boundary narrow, pass serializable data, define personalized cache behavior explicitly, and avoid hydrating the whole page for one interactive region.
followUpPrompts: What changes if price is user-specific?
Where does cart state live?
mayaPushbacks: Why does that region need JavaScript?
What can be cached across users?

scoringRubric.strong: Boundaries follow interactivity and data constraints with explicit caching.
scoringRubric.developing: Reasonable split but cache or hydration is vague.

templates.title: Client cache consistency
templates.prompt: Design cache keys, freshness, invalidation, and background refresh for a dashboard whose filters and permissions change the result set.
templates.objective: Build a cache identity and freshness policy that cannot mix filters, users, or stale mutation results.
hints: A cache key must include every input that changes the response.
Separate how long data may be reused from when a background refresh should begin.
templates.explanation: Normalize filter and identity inputs into stable cache keys, scope permission-sensitive data per user, define stale and retention windows, cancel or ignore obsolete requests, and invalidate or patch affected keys after mutation.
goodAnswerSignals: Includes filters and identity in keys
weakAnswerSignals: Says refetch everything without consistency rules
followUpPrompts: What happens on rapid filter changes?
How do two tabs converge?
mayaPushbacks: Which input changes the identity of this result?
What makes stale data safe here?

scoringRubric.strong: Complete cache identity and consistency policy.
scoringRubric.developing: Good keys but weak invalidation or race behavior.

templates.title: Optimistic updates and idempotency
templates.prompt: Design an optimistic comment action that survives retries, duplicate clicks, rejection, and a server response arriving after the user edits again.
templates.objective: Coordinate optimistic identity, idempotent mutation requests, rollback, and out-of-order acknowledgements.
hints: Give the optimistic entity and mutation a client-generated identity.
A rollback must not erase a newer user action that replaced the rejected state.
templates.explanation: Create a stable client mutation ID, insert a pending entity, deduplicate the request server-side, reconcile the authoritative response by identity, and roll back only the rejected version. Track mutation order so an older acknowledgement cannot overwrite newer state.
weakAnswerSignals: Restores a whole old cache snapshot on any failure
followUpPrompts: How does offline replay work?
What if moderation changes the text?
mayaPushbacks: Which operation is the server deduplicating?
Can this rollback delete a newer edit?

answerStructure.framework: Identity → optimistic state → server dedupe → reconcile

scoringRubric.strong: Correct under retry, rejection, and response reordering.
scoringRubric.developing: Optimistic happy path but weak concurrency.

templates.title: Evolving a design system safely
templates.prompt: Design how a shared component library can change tokens and component APIs across many applications without silent visual or accessibility regressions.
templates.objective: Define ownership, contracts, versioning, migration, testing, and rollout for a multi-consumer design system.
hints: Separate stable semantic contracts from implementation and visual tokens.
Think about how consumers discover, test, migrate, and roll back a breaking change.
templates.explanation: Use semantic tokens and constrained component APIs, document compatibility, automate visual/accessibility/contract tests, publish changes with clear versioning and codemods, observe adoption, and support phased rollout and rollback.
weakAnswerSignals: Publishes breaking CSS globally without migration
followUpPrompts: Who approves a breaking change?
How do you find risky consumers?
mayaPushbacks: What contract are consumers relying on?
How does a team roll back?

scoringRubric.strong: Treats the design system as a governed platform with safe evolution.
scoringRubric.developing: Good components but weak release mechanics.

templates.title: Large-list rendering architecture
templates.prompt: Design a searchable table with hundreds of thousands of rows, variable row heights, keyboard navigation, and live updates.
templates.objective: Balance data-windowing, DOM virtualization, interaction correctness, accessibility, and live-update consistency.
hints: There are two windows: which records are fetched and which DOM rows are mounted.
Keyboard focus and screen-reader context must survive virtualization.
templates.explanation: Use server-side filtering and paged cursors, virtualize the rendered window with measured heights and overscan, preserve stable row identity and focus, merge live updates by version, and expose accessible position and loading semantics.
weakAnswerSignals: Virtualizes without keyboard or accessibility behavior
followUpPrompts: How do variable heights affect scroll position?
How is selection preserved?
mayaPushbacks: How many DOM nodes exist?
Where does focus go when a row unmounts?

answerStructure.framework: Data window → render window → identity → interaction

scoringRubric.strong: Scales data and DOM while preserving interaction correctness.
scoringRubric.developing: Performance works but accessibility or live updates are vague.
scoringRubric.weak: Renders everything or loses user state.

templates.title: Offline drafts and recovery
templates.prompt: Design offline draft editing and eventual synchronization for a web application where the same document may change on another device.
templates.objective: Define local durability, queue identity, retry, conflict detection, merge policy, and transparent recovery UX.
hints: Separate the cached application shell, durable local draft, and queued server mutation.
A retry policy cannot resolve two valid edits to the same version by itself.
templates.explanation: Persist versioned drafts locally, queue idempotent mutations, replay with backoff when connected, compare base versions on the server, and surface a merge or conflict workflow when automatic reconciliation is unsafe. Service workers help delivery but do not define conflict semantics.
followUpPrompts: What is safe to merge automatically?
How is a failed queue item visible?
mayaPushbacks: What version was this draft based on?
Who resolves two valid edits?

answerStructure.framework: Persist → queue → replay → detect conflict → recover

scoringRubric.strong: Complete durability and conflict model with transparent recovery.
scoringRubric.developing: Offline queue exists but conflict semantics are weak.

templates.title: Observable frontend release system
templates.prompt: Design a release and observability system for a high-traffic web application so the team can detect, contain, and safely reverse frontend regressions.
templates.objective: Connect release identity, client telemetry, user-impact signals, progressive delivery, alerting, and rollback into one operable design.
hints: Every client error and performance signal should identify the exact release and important user context.
Separate a technical signal from the product impact that should trigger containment.
templates.explanation: Stamp telemetry with release and feature-flag versions, collect sampled errors, web vitals, failed journeys, and backend correlation IDs, then compare canary cohorts against a baseline. Use impact-based alerts, kill switches, progressive rollout, and an automated or operator-approved rollback path with source maps and runbooks for diagnosis.
followUpPrompts: Which signals block a rollout?
How do you distinguish a frontend failure from an API failure?
mayaPushbacks: How do you know this release caused it?
What can be disabled without another deploy?

scoringRubric.strong: Treats delivery and observability as one closed-loop reliability system.
scoringRubric.developing: Useful telemetry but weak rollout or rollback mechanics.
scoringRubric.weak: Tool list without release correlation or containment.
